10-07.text: The military wing of the Palestinian nationalist Islamist political organization Hamas massacred people attending an open-air music festival in southern Israel.

10-08.text: Marxist revolutionary and guerrilla leader Che Guevara was captured near La Higuera, Bolivia.

10-09.title: Treaty of Bern
10-09.text: The Universal Postal Union, then known as the General Postal Union, was established with the signing of the Treaty of Bern to unify disparate postal services and regulations so that international mail could be exchanged easily.
10-09.alt: 1874: Treaty of Bern. The Universal Postal Union, then known as the General Postal Union, was established with the signing of the Treaty of Bern to unify disparate postal services and regulations so that international mail could be exchanged easily.

10-10.title: Women's Social and Political Union
10-10.text: Emmeline Pankhurst founded the Women's Social and Political Union, a militant organisation campaigning for women's suffrage in the United Kingdom.
10-10.alt: 1903: Women's Social and Political Union. Emmeline Pankhurst founded the Women's Social and Political Union, a militant organisation campaigning for women's suffrage in the United Kingdom.

10-11.title: Apollo 7
10-11.text: Apollo 7, the first manned mission of NASA's Apollo program, and the first three-man American space mission, launched from Complex 34 in Cape Kennedy, Florida.

10-12.title: Nikita Khrushchev
10-12.text: Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev reportedly pounded his shoe on a desk during a meeting of the United Nations General Assembly in protest at a speech by Philippine delegate Lorenzo Sumulong.

10-13.title: Brigid Kosgei
10-13.text: At the Chicago Marathon, Kenyan runner Brigid Kosgei set the current marathon world record for women running in a mixed-sex race.
10-13.alt: 2019: Brigid Kosgei. At the Chicago Marathon, Kenyan runner Brigid Kosgei set the current marathon world record for women running in a mixed-sex race.

10-14.title: Winnie-the-Pooh (book)
10-14.text: The first book featuring English author A. A. Milne's fictional bear Winnie-the-Pooh was published.

10-15.title: 15 October 2011 global protests
10-15.text: Global demonstrations against economic inequality, corporate influence on government, and other issues, were held in more than 950 cities in 82 countries.

10-16.title: The Chronicles of Narnia
10-16.text: The first novel of the The Chronicles of Narnia series by C. S. Lewis, The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, was published in the United Kingdom.

10-17.title: The Open Championship
10-17.text: The Open Championship, the oldest of the four major championships in men's golf, was first played at Prestwick Golf Club in Scotland.

10-18.title: Renton F.C.
10-18.text: Renton defeated Kilmarnock 2–0 in the opening match of the inaugural Scottish Cup.

10-19.title: YouTube
10-19.text: British YouTube collective the Sidemen were formed as a Rockstar Games Social Club group in Grand Theft Auto Online.

10-20.title: Watergate scandal
10-20.text: Watergate scandal: Attorney General Elliot Richardson and his deputy William Ruckelshaus resigned after refusing to obey President Richard Nixon's order to have Archibald Cox fired.

10-21.title: Medicine Lodge, Kansas
10-21.text: The first and second of three treaties were signed near Medicine Lodge, Kansas, between the United States federal government and several Native American tribes in the Great Plains, requiring them to relocate to areas in present-day western Oklahoma.

10-22.title: Ian Fleming
10-22.text: The first volume of Ian Fleming's children's novel Chitty-Chitty-Bang-Bang was published posthumously.

10-23.title: Grand Theft Auto III
10-23.text: Grand Theft Auto III was released, helping to popularize open-world and mature-content video games.

10-24.title: 1975 Icelandic women's strike
10-24.text: In protest against wage discrepancy and unfair employment practices, 90 percent of Iceland's female population went on strike for a day.
10-24.alt: 1975: 1975 Icelandic women's strike. In protest against wage discrepancy and unfair employment practices, 90 percent of Iceland's female population went on strike for a day.

10-25.title: Mount Merapi
10-25.text: Mount Merapi in Central Java, Indonesia, began an increasingly violent series of eruptions that lasted over a month.

10-26.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
10-26.text: Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, considered one of the best video games ever made, in North America.

10-27.title: New York City Subway
10-27.text: The first underground segment of the New York City Subway opened, connecting New York City Hall with Harlem.
10-27.alt: 1904: New York City Subway. The first underground segment of the New York City Subway opened, connecting New York City Hall with Harlem.

10-28.title: United States Declaration of Independence
10-28.text: In New York Harbor, U.S. president Grover Cleveland dedicated the Statue of Liberty, a gift from France commemorating the Declaration of Independence.
10-28.alt: 1886: United States Declaration of Independence. In New York Harbor, U.S. president Grover Cleveland dedicated the Statue of Liberty, a gift from France commemorating the Declaration of Independence.

10-29.title: Galileo (spacecraft)
10-29.text: Galileo became the first spacecraft to visit an asteroid when it made a flyby of 951 Gaspra.

10-30.title: Michael Jackson
10-30.text: Michael Jackson released Invincible, his final studio album and the most expensive album ever produced.
10-30.alt: 2001: Michael Jackson. Michael Jackson released Invincible, his final studio album and the most expensive album ever produced.

10-31.title: Hubble Space Telescope
10-31.text: The discovery of the Plutonian moons Nix and Hydra, based on photographs taken by the Hubble Space Telescope nearly five months prior, was announced.

11-01.title: Ansel Adams
11-01.text: American photographer Ansel Adams shot Moonrise, Hernandez, New Mexico, one of his most famous photographs.
11-01.alt: 1941: Ansel Adams. American photographer Ansel Adams shot Moonrise, Hernandez, New Mexico, one of his most famous photographs.

11-02.title: James A. Garfield
11-02.text: James A. Garfield was elected as president of the United States; the election is the closest to date by popular vote margin.

11-03.title: Mapuche
11-03.text: Indigenous Mapuche began an uprising against the occupation of Araucanía by Chile.

11-04.title: Túpac Amaru II
11-04.text: Túpac Amaru II led a rebellion of Aymara, Quechua, and mestizo peasants in protest against the Bourbon Reforms in the Spanish Viceroyalty of Peru.

11-05.title: Mars Orbiter Mission
11-05.text: The Indian Space Research Organisation launched the Mars Orbiter Mission, India's first interplanetary probe.
11-05.alt: 2013: Mars Orbiter Mission. The Indian Space Research Organisation launched the Mars Orbiter Mission, India's first interplanetary probe.

11-06.title: Red Cloud
11-06.text: Red Cloud, a Native American leader of the Oglala Lakota tribe, signed the Treaty of Fort Laramie, ending Red Cloud's War and establishing the Great Sioux Reservation.

11-07.title: Magic Johnson
11-07.text: Magic Johnson announced his retirement from professional basketball due to HIV infection.
11-07.alt: 1991: Magic Johnson. Magic Johnson announced his retirement from professional basketball due to HIV infection.

11-08.title: Federal Intelligence Service
11-08.text: German newspaper Der Spiegel publishes a report by the Federal Intelligence Service accusing figures in Liechtenstein of cooperating with organized crime.

11-09.title: Rolling Stone
11-09.text: The first issue of Rolling Stone, an American magazine focusing on music, politics and popular culture, was published.
11-09.alt: 1967: Rolling Stone. The first issue of Rolling Stone, an American magazine focusing on music, politics and popular culture, was published.

11-10.title: Nadarajah Raviraj
11-10.text: Nadarajah Raviraj, a prominent Sri Lankan Tamil politician and human rights lawyer, was assassinated in Colombo.
11-10.alt: 2006: Nadarajah Raviraj. Nadarajah Raviraj, a prominent Sri Lankan Tamil politician and human rights lawyer, was assassinated in Colombo.

11-11.title: American Revolutionary War
11-11.text: American Revolutionary War: British forces and their Iroquois allies attacked a fort and the village of Cherry Valley, New York, killing 14 soldiers and 30 civilians.

11-12.title: Allegheny Athletic Association
11-12.text: William Heffelfinger was paid $500 by the Allegheny Athletic Association, becoming the first professional American football player.

11-13.title: Walt Disney
11-13.text: Walt Disney's Fantasia, the first commercial film shown with stereophonic sound, premiered at the Broadway Theatre in New York City.
11-13.alt: 1940: Walt Disney. Walt Disney's Fantasia, the first commercial film shown with stereophonic sound, premiered at the Broadway Theatre in New York City.

11-14.title: Kennedy Space Center
11-14.text: Apollo 12 launched from the Kennedy Space Center, later becoming the second crewed flight to land on the Moon.

11-15.title: Evangelos Zappas
11-15.text: Sponsored by Greek businessman Evangelos Zappas, the first modern revival of the Olympic Games took place in Athens.

11-16.title: North-West Rebellion
11-16.text: After a five-day trial following the North-West Rebellion, Louis Riel, a Canadian Métis leader and "Father of Manitoba", was hanged for high treason.

11-17.title: NBC
11-17.text: NBC controversially cut away from an American football game between the Oakland Raiders and New York Jets to broadcast Heidi, causing viewers in the Eastern United States to miss the game's dramatic ending.

11-18.title: Minecraft
11-18.text: The sandbox video game Minecraft exited beta with the official release of version 1.0.
11-18.alt: 2011: Minecraft. The sandbox video game Minecraft exited beta with the official release of version 1.0.

11-19.title: Pelé
11-19.text: Playing for Santos against Vasco da Gama in Rio de Janeiro, Brazilian footballer Pelé scored his thousandth goal.
11-19.alt: 1969: Pelé. Playing for Santos against Vasco da Gama in Rio de Janeiro, Brazilian footballer Pelé scored his thousandth goal.

11-20.title: Essex (whaleship)
11-20.text: The American whaleship Essex sank 2,000 nautical miles (3,700 km) west of the western coast of South America after it was attacked by a sperm whale, an event which inspired the novel Moby-Dick by Herman Melville.

11-21.title: Valemount
11-21.text: Two trains collided near Valemount, Canada, killing 21 people; the subsequent trial brought future prime minister John Diefenbaker to greater political attention.

11-22.title: Toy Story
11-22.text: Toy Story, the first feature film created using only computer-generated imagery, was released in theaters in the United States.
11-22.alt: 1995: Toy Story. Toy Story, the first feature film created using only computer-generated imagery, was released in theaters in the United States.

11-23.title: Rose Revolution
11-23.text: Rose Revolution: Eduard Shevardnadze resigned as President of Georgia following weeks of mass protests over disputed election results.

11-24.title: Charles Darwin
11-24.text: British naturalist Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species was first published, and sold out its initial print run on the first day.
11-24.alt: 1859: Charles Darwin. British naturalist Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species was first published, and sold out its initial print run on the first day.

11-25.title: One Direction
11-25.text: English-Irish boy band One Direction released their third studio album Midnight Memories which debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 and became the best-selling album of 2013.

11-26.title: Mars Science Laboratory
11-26.text: NASA launched the Mars Science Laboratory mission from Cape Canaveral, carrying the Curiosity rover on board.
11-26.alt: 2011: Mars Science Laboratory. NASA launched the Mars Science Laboratory mission from Cape Canaveral, carrying the Curiosity rover on board.

11-27.title: Medellín Cartel
11-27.text: A bomb placed by the Medellín Cartel in an attempt to kill Colombian presidential candidate César Gaviria destroyed Avianca Flight 203, killing all 107 people on board, excluding Gaviria, who was not on the flight.

11-28.title: Piano Concerto No. 5 (Beethoven)
11-28.text: Beethoven's Piano Concerto No. 5 premiered at the Gewandhaus in Leipzig.

11-29.title: Michael Jackson
11-29.text: Michael Jackson's Thriller, the best-selling album of all time, was released.
11-29.alt: 1982: Michael Jackson. Michael Jackson's Thriller, the best-selling album of all time, was released.

11-30.title: Texas
11-30.text: A college football game between the SMU Mustangs and the TCU Horned Frogs became the first game in Texas to be broadcast nationally on radio.

12-01.title: Rosa Parks
12-01.text: Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing to give up her seat on a public bus to a white man in Montgomery, Alabama, United States, sparking the Montgomery bus boycott.
12-01.alt: 1955: Rosa Parks. Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing to give up her seat on a public bus to a white man in Montgomery, Alabama, United States, sparking the Montgomery bus boycott.

12-02.title: Pablo Escobar
12-02.text: Colombian National Police killed Pablo Escobar on a Medellín rooftop, ending the long manhunt for the Medellín Cartel boss.
12-02.alt: 1993: Pablo Escobar. Colombian National Police killed Pablo Escobar on a Medellín rooftop, ending the long manhunt for the Medellín Cartel boss.

12-03.title: Sony Interactive Entertainment
12-03.text: Sony released the PlayStation, the first computer entertainment platform to ship 100 million units.
12-03.alt: 1994: Sony Interactive Entertainment. Sony released the PlayStation, the first computer entertainment platform to ship 100 million units.

12-04.title: Black Panther Party
12-04.text: Fred Hampton, the leader of the Illinois chapter of the Black Panther Party, and Mark Clark were killed in a raid by Chicago police officers in what many scholars consider an illegal assassination.
12-04.alt: 1969: Black Panther Party. Fred Hampton, the leader of the Illinois chapter of the Black Panther Party, and Mark Clark were killed in a raid by Chicago police officers in what many scholars consider an illegal assassination.

12-05.title: Glasnost meeting
12-05.text: The "glasnost meeting" took place in Moscow, becoming the first demonstration in the Soviet Union after World War II and marking the beginning of the civil rights movement in the country.
12-05.alt: 1965: Glasnost meeting. The "glasnost meeting" took place in Moscow, becoming the first demonstration in the Soviet Union after World War II and marking the beginning of the civil rights movement in the country.

12-06.title: Slavery in the United States
12-06.text: Slavery in the United States was officially abolished with the ratification of the Thirteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution.
12-06.alt: 1865: Slavery in the United States. Slavery in the United States was officially abolished with the ratification of the Thirteenth Amendment to the U.S.

12-07.title: Galileo (spacecraft)
12-07.text: The Galileo spacecraft arrived at Jupiter, a little more than six years after it was launched by Space Shuttle Atlantis during Mission STS-34.

12-08.title: Metallica
12-08.text: Metallica played a concert in Antarctica, becoming the first band to perform on all seven continents.

12-09.title: Mumia Abu-Jamal
12-09.text: Mumia Abu-Jamal was arrested for the murder of Philadelphia police officer Daniel Faulkner; his subsequent conviction and death sentence generated controversy in the United States.

12-10.title: First-person shooter
12-10.text: The video game Doom, later considered the "father" of the first-person shooter genre, is released.
12-10.alt: 1993: First-person shooter. The video game Doom, later considered the "father" of the first-person shooter genre, is released.

12-11.title: Mexican drug war
12-11.text: The first action in the Mexican drug war began as President Felipe Calderón ordered Mexican soldiers and Federal Police units into the state of Michoacán.

12-12.title: Greek junta
12-12.text: The Greek junta announced its withdrawal from the Council of Europe after the junta was found guilty of torture and other human-rights violations by the European Commission of Human Rights.
12-12.alt: 1969: Greek junta. The Greek junta announced its withdrawal from the Council of Europe after the junta was found guilty of torture and other human-rights violations by the European Commission of Human Rights.

12-13.title: Beyoncé
12-13.text: Beyoncé released her fifth studio album without any prior announcement or promotion; it sold 2.3 million copies before the end of the year.
12-13.alt: 2013: Beyoncé. Beyoncé released her fifth studio album without any prior announcement or promotion; it sold 2.3 million copies before the end of the year.

12-14.title: Apollo 17
12-14.text: Upon completing the third extra-vehicular activity of Apollo 17, American astronaut Gene Cernan became the last person to date to walk on the Moon.

12-15.title: Citizenship Amendment Act protests
12-15.text: Citizenship Amendment Act protests: 10 to 15 local women blockaded a major road in Delhi, India, to protest the exclusion of Muslims from the amended Citizenship Act.
12-15.alt: 2019: Citizenship Amendment Act protests. Citizenship Amendment Act protests: 10 to 15 local women blockaded a major road in Delhi, India, to protest the exclusion of Muslims from the amended Citizenship Act.

12-16.title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
12-16.text: The Parliament of England enacted the Bill of Rights, setting out basic civil rights and later influencing other documents such as the U.S. Bill of Rights and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
12-16.alt: 1689: Universal Declaration of Human Rights. The Parliament of England enacted the Bill of Rights, setting out basic civil rights and later influencing other documents such as the U.S.

12-17.title: Arab Spring
12-17.text: Arab Spring: Mohamed Bouazizi, a street vendor in Sidi Bouzid, set himself on fire in protest against police harassment, triggering the Tunisian revolution.

12-18.title: The Jew's Christmas
12-18.text: The Jew's Christmas, the first American film to include a rabbi as a character, was released.

12-19.title: Titanic (1997 film)
12-19.text: Titanic, the fourth-highest-grossing film of all time with a worldwide total of more than US$2.2 billion, was released in the United States.
12-19.alt: 1997: Titanic (1997 film). Titanic, the fourth-highest-grossing film of all time with a worldwide total of more than US$2.2 billion, was released in the United States.

12-20.title: Captain America
12-20.text: The superhero Captain America made his first published appearance in the comic book Captain America Comics #1.

12-21.title: Kennedy Space Center
12-21.text: Apollo 8 launched from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on a trajectory to the Moon; its crew became the first humans to visit another celestial body.

12-22.title: Richard Reid
12-22.text: Richard Reid unsuccessfully attempted to detonate a bomb in his shoe on a transatlantic flight from Paris to Miami.

12-23.title: Jane Austen
12-23.text: Jane Austen's novel Emma was first published, the last novel released during her lifetime.

12-24.title: Jim Lovell
12-24.text: Piloted by Jim Lovell, Apollo 8 became the first human spaceflight to reach and orbit the Moon.

12-25.title: Tim Berners-Lee
12-25.text: British computer programmer Tim Berners-Lee introduced WorldWideWeb, the world's first web browser and WYSIWYG HTML editor.
12-25.alt: 1990: Tim Berners-Lee. British computer programmer Tim Berners-Lee introduced WorldWideWeb, the world's first web browser and WYSIWYG HTML editor.

12-26.title: Submarine communications cable
12-26.text: Two earthquakes off the southwest coast of Taiwan damaged submarine communications cables, disrupting Internet services in Asia and affecting financial transactions.
12-26.alt: 2006: Submarine communications cable. Two earthquakes off the southwest coast of Taiwan damaged submarine communications cables, disrupting Internet services in Asia and affecting financial transactions.

12-27.title: Tehran
12-27.text: During protests in Tehran against the recent presidential election, Iranian security forces opened fire on demonstrators.

12-28.title: Black Mirror: Bandersnatch
12-28.text: Netflix released Black Mirror: Bandersnatch, its first interactive content for adults.

12-29.title: Wounded Knee Massacre
12-29.text: Sioux Wars: The United States Army killed 250 to 300 Lakota men, women and children at the Wounded Knee Massacre, beginning the Ghost Dance War.
12-29.alt: 1890: Wounded Knee Massacre. Sioux Wars: The United States Army killed 250 to 300 Lakota men, women and children at the Wounded Knee Massacre, beginning the Ghost Dance War.

12-30.title: Saddam Hussein
12-30.text: Saddam Hussein, the former president of Iraq, was executed after being found guilty of crimes against humanity by the Iraqi High Tribunal.

12-31.title: Roberto Clemente
12-31.text: Puerto Rican baseball player Roberto Clemente died in a plane crash en route to deliver aid to victims of that year's Nicaragua earthquake.
12-31.alt: 1972: Roberto Clemente. Puerto Rican baseball player Roberto Clemente died in a plane crash en route to deliver aid to victims of that year's Nicaragua earthquake.
